metadata.title: Teachers' expectancy-value-cost profiles in professional development to support students’ self-regulated learning

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses a convenience sample of 171 teachers nested within 10 Estonian schools participating in a year-long SRL-focused professional development program. The analysis is based on repeated self-report measures across four waves (T1–T4) and does not describe the use of TALIS/PISA-style sampling weights or any complex survey design variables. Because the outcomes are questionnaire-based constructs (teaching practices, expectancies, values, and multidimensional perceived costs) and the authors do not report applying any sampling/replicate weights, the results should be interpreted as descriptive/associational within this program sample rather than population-representative estimates. Missingness is handled via FIML for wave-specific modeling and mean-computation at the item level, while longitudinal comparisons use pairwise deletion; no weight-based variance estimation is reported.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values are not applicable because the study does not analyze ILSA cognitive achievement scores generated via PVs; instead, it models teachers’ self-reported questionnaire constructs (SRL-related teaching practices, expectancies, subjective task values, and perceived cost dimensions). Missing data handling is described (FIML for wave-specific modeling and pairwise deletion for longitudinal analyses), so the missing-data strategy is not a reporting gap; however, the schema mapping treats FIML as multiple-imputation-like handling.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used a convenience sample of 171 teachers nested within 10 Estonian schools participating in a year-long SRL-focused professional development program organized by Teach for Estonia and Tallinn University. Teachers provided self-evaluations of SRL-related teaching practices at T1 (N=136) and T4 (N=118), and motivation measures at T2 (N=138) and T3 (N=116); response rates varied by wave due to absence/attrition. Missing item responses were handled by computing composite scores as the mean of available items (only two missing values in the entire dataset), and longitudinal analyses used pairwise deletion; wave-specific modeling used Full Information Maximum Likelihood (FIML). Background demographic variables were collected at T1 (N=136) and were tested for confounding, but were excluded from main analyses when inconsistent.

main_findings.dataset_used: Longitudinal SRL-focused PD (Estonia, 2023/24; teacher questionnaire; waves T1–T4)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Paired samples t-tests: all five practice factors increased from T1 to T4 (PM2 vs PM1: t(86)=8.67, p<.001, Cohen's d=0.93; ES2 vs ES1: t(86)=5.01, p<.001, d=0.54; CS2 vs CS1: t(86)=4.00, p<.001, d=0.43; SC2 vs SC1: t(86)=4.80, p<.001, d=0.52; CE2 vs CE1: t(86)=3.56, p<.001, d=0.38).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using longitudinal SRL-focused PD data from Estonia (teacher questionnaire; waves T1–T4), the study leveraged expectancy for success, subjective task value, and multiple perceived cost dimensions to examine SRL-related teaching practices, finding that all five practice factors significantly increased from the beginning to the end of the program. This indicates that SRL-related professional development is associated with teachers reporting greater implementation of SRL-supportive practices over time, though the absence of a control group limits causal claims.

main_findings.dataset_used: Longitudinal SRL-focused PD (Estonia, 2023/24; teacher questionnaire; waves T1–T4)
main_findings.target_variable: Associations between motivation/cost and SRL-related teaching practices
main_findings.performance_metrics: Correlations (selected): At program beginning, expectancy correlated positively with PM1 (r=.33, p<.001) and ES1 (r=.31, p<.01), but not with CS1/SC1/CE1; value correlated positively with PM1 (r=.23, p<.05) and ES1 (r=.32, p<.01). Cost dimensions showed mostly negative relations: task effort correlated negatively with PM2 (r=-.24, p<.05) and ES2 (r=-.21, p<.05) and outside effort correlated negatively with PM2 (r=-.27, p<.01) and SC2 (r=-.26, p<.05). At the end of the program, expectancy2 correlated positively with PM2 (r=.37, p<.001), ES2 (r=.36, p<.001), CS2 (r=.31, p<.001), and CE2 (r=.30, p<.001), while outside effort2 correlated negatively with PM2 (r=-.35, p<.001).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using longitudinal SRL-focused PD data from Estonia (teacher questionnaire; waves T1–T4), the study leveraged teachers’ expectancies, subjective task values, and multidimensional perceived costs to relate motivation to SRL-related teaching practices, finding predominantly positive associations for expectancies/values and sporadic but meaningful negative associations for perceived costs—especially outside effort and task effort—most consistently predicting end-of-program practices. This indicates that PD designers should prioritize interventions that strengthen teachers’ expectancy for success and reduce perceived implementation costs (particularly time/effort outside PD), while recognizing that these are correlational findings from self-reports without causal identification.

main_findings.dataset_used: Longitudinal SRL-focused PD (Estonia, 2023/24; teacher questionnaire; LPA at T1 and T4)
main_findings.target_variable: Motivational profile membership and SRL-related teaching practices
main_findings.performance_metrics: Latent Profile Analysis selected 2 classes at both time points. At T1, initially less motivated profile comprised 29% and initially more motivated 71%; Welch's ANOVA showed lower practice for initially less motivated teachers in PM (p=.004) and ES (p=.050) at the beginning, and at T4 they reported significantly lower PM, ES, SC, and CE (end-of-program differences in four of five factors). At T4, eventually less motivated profile comprised 46% and eventually more motivated 54%; Welch's ANOVA found no significant differences at T1 practices, but significant end-of-program differences for PM (p=.040) and ES (p=.014). Profile stability across T2/T3: 78.4% remained in a similar profile type.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using longitudinal SRL-focused PD data from Estonia (teacher questionnaire; latent profile analysis at the beginning and end of the program), the study leveraged expectancies, subjective task values, and multidimensional perceived costs to identify two motivational profiles and linked them to SRL-related teaching practices, finding that initially less motivated teachers implemented fewer SRL-supportive practices and that end-of-program differences were most evident for metacognition promotion and emotional support. This indicates that targeted PD support may be most effective when it identifies teachers with lower expectancies/values and higher perceived costs early, then provides structured support to improve both motivation and perceived feasibility of SRL integration.

data.outcome_summary: This study used a longitudinal teacher-survey design embedded in a year-long SRL-focused professional development program in Estonia (2023/24), collecting data at four waves (T1–T4) from teachers nested in 10 schools. The analytic sample comprised 171 teachers initially, with wave-specific Ns of 136 (T1), 138 (T2), 116 (T3), and 118 (T4). Teachers’ SRL-related teaching practices increased significantly from T1 to T4 across all five practice factors (e.g., promoting metacognition: t(86)=8.67, p<.001, d=0.93; emotional support: t(86)=5.01, p<.001, d=0.54). Motivation and perceived costs showed mostly positive associations for expectancies/values and sporadic negative associations for cost dimensions, with outside effort showing particularly strong negative correlations with end-of-program practices. The study relies on self-reports and has no control group, so effects cannot be interpreted causally; additionally, it does not use ILSA plausible values or survey weights.
